local_origin_utm.note: CENTRE of the bbox in UTM 43N. Chosen over the SW corner so runtime coords are symmetric (about +/-2000 m), the camera orbits the true origin, and float32 precision headroom is maximised.

study_area.clip: All geometry is clipped to the bbox. Overpass returns complete ways, which spilled up to 760 m outside the box before clipping. Buildings are kept or dropped whole by centroid (they are small, so no visible seam); ground polygons and all lines are cut at the boundary.

tiles.role: SPATIAL INDEX ONLY — not an asset-splitting scheme. Spike-0 measured ~96k triangles of ordinary buildings for the whole box, so per-tile GLBs were dropped as over-engineering. Tiles remain the lookup key for entity picking and corridor metrics.

corridors.label: Kartavya Path
corridors.no_transit_reason: A ceremonial boulevard — no bus route runs on it. Spike-0 measured 0 of 210 OSM bus route relations touching it. The bus-frequency scenario must visibly disable itself here with this reason stated, never silently return zero.

required.note: Published monument height (42 m). OSM carries no height tag for way/361709652.
Circular colonnade. Replaces the proposed 'Sansad Bhavan', which does not exist in OSM under that name.

Rajiv Chowk Central Park plus the colonnaded inner ring around it — modelled as a ring, not one building. Rajiv Chowk Central Park is open ground, not a building. The colonnaded inner ring around it is separate building stock and is already in the buildings layer.

optional.note: The OSM footprint is the walled enclosure, not the masonry instruments inside it. Rendering it as a block would misrepresent the site.

landmarks.kind_note: kind=massing extrudes the verified footprint; kind=open renders as a flat plaza or lawn with a label and no massing. Heights resolve in order: OSM height tag (observed) -> assumed_height_m from a published dimension (estimated) -> none.

order: satellite median building height (Open Buildings 2.5D) -> remote_sensed
height_rule.disclosure: Height provenance is shown in the UI in three states, not two: observed from an OSM tag, measured from satellite, or estimated by class rule. v0.1 left 91.8% of the box on an authored guess; v0.2 puts most of it on a measurement with a published 1.5 m MAE, and the remaining estimated share is named in the buildings layer provenance rather than footnoted.

remote_sensed.dataset: Google Research Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal v1, band building_height
remote_sensed.attribution: Building heights (c) Google Research Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal, derived from Copernicus Sentinel-2
remote_sensed.statistic: median of footprint pixels above 1 m
remote_sensed._why_median: Five statistics were scored against the 241 buildings in this box holding a real OSM height tag, stratified by height band. The median of positive pixels has the flattest bias across 0-45 m, where 213 of them sit. Chosen for low bias rather than lowest MAE: in a 3D city, systematic bias distorts the skyline and misplaces every shadow, while scatter averages out over 3,000 buildings.

measured_against_osm._caveat: The OSM height sample is selection-biased towards tall and notable buildings (its p90 is 45.5 m, which is not central Delhi), so the per-band table is the honest read and the overall figure flatters both estimators.

remote_sensed.known_limitation: Above 45 m this under-reads by 12-18 m. Sentinel-2 derived heights saturate on towers. Uncorrected on purpose: the sample showing the bias is 28 buildings.

initial_transfer_mb.note: Target cut from 12 to 6 MB after Spike-0 measured the real geometry volume. The 15 MB PRD gate stays as the hard ceiling.

budgets._gpu_note: GPU milliseconds, measured with EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 at a parked camera. This is the budget that actually limits visual quality, and it was invisible until instrumented: CPU frame time read 1.4 ms while the GPU was spending 19. Two findings came straight out of it — the shadow map was 73% of GPU time (fixed by rendering it on demand rather than every frame, 10.1 ms reclaimed), and screen-space AO cost ~18 ms and doubled submitted geometry, so it is opt-in only and the AO comes from a Blender bake instead. Note headless reports devicePixelRatio 1; a Retina display is 4x the pixels, so a headless pass is necessary but not sufficient.

_measured.device: Apple M1 / 8 GB, ANGLE Metal, 1600x913 at dpr 1

_history.note: The wide view was 10.8 ms earlier on 2026-09-03, before the reach, routes and street furniture layers. It then read 33.1 ms, and altitude gates on rooftop detail, street furniture and pedestrians brought it to 19.4 ms with a 1% repeat spread. It is still OVER the 16.7 ms budget and the gate is red.

_measured._instability_warning: This device drifts by up to 2x within a single session under sustained load: the SAME commit measured 12.9 ms and then 21-25 ms at the same camera an hour apart, and one build read 23.3 then 41.3 ms in consecutive passes. A single sample is not evidence. tools/qa.mjs therefore measures each camera twice and takes the LOWER median - contention and throttling can only add time to a frame, never remove it - and prints the repeat spread so an unstable machine is visible. Note that a small spread does NOT prove the machine is healthy: a sustained-throttled GPU is stably slow. Every absolute figure here wants re-measuring on a cool device.

health.note: No live provider is REQUIRED. Every layer in this manifest is bundled and the guided demo completes with all adapters disabled. Anything listed here is additive: the app only contacts a provider named in this list, so a build without a key never fires a request that cannot succeed.
health.env_note: Adapters needing a credential stay FALSE in the committed config, because a clone without the key would fire requests that can only fail. They are enabled per build from the environment instead: this build found the variables listed in live_adapters_from_env. The committed scope lock is therefore the same for everyone, and what a given deployment actually contacts is a property of that deployment.
